text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Laos and Myanmar become ASEAN members, signifying formal return to mainstream of Southeast Asian nations after decades of isolation.
- Poor performers in Civil Service must buck up or be prepared to lose jobs, Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong says.
- Police detain 206 suspected illegal immigrants hiding in forested areas and lodging houses during islandwide raid in past two days.
- Private non-landed home prices slip another 1.6 percent on average two months after end of first quarter.
- Diversified conglomerate Sembawang Corp finally makes takeover offer for Jurong Shipyard Ltd after mulling over details for more than six months.

- Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan sends stocks and bonds soaring on Tuesday when he suggests he is in no hurry to push U.S. borrowing costs higher as economy continues on "exceptional" path of high growth and low inflation.
- There will be no raising of 80 percent limit on housing loans, says Finance Minister Richard Hu yesterday in Parliament.

- U.S. dollar issues spring back into favour in local stock market after two-day break, while firm demand for electronics counters pushes Sesdaq to 3-year high and SES Electronics Index to all-time record.
- After cornering deli market here, Delifrance is taking its market strategy to region.
- Jack Chia MPH Ltd, Singapore publishing and confectionery company, says it agreed to buy Indonesian candy company for Singapore $8.3 million.
- Property developer First Capital Corp proposing S$150 million bond issue to finance development projects and refinance bonds maturing this year.
